verdict.why: Option Y is the more complete and buildable implementation specification. Design 1 explicitly reviews the spec loop, research, council, planning, build and remaining HTTP call sites, while C1-C7 define concrete configuration, CLIs, validation rules, ledger rows, summaries, warnings and exit codes, with T1-T24 covering them. It also follows two literal requirements that X relaxes without support: REQ-4 permits exactly one HTTP request per validator with no retry, whereas X/D11 can issue a second request; and Y applies the paid thinker/writer split to every size, whereas X/D3 invents a size-S exemption despite the order giving none. Y's finally-appended spend rows, O_APPEND/flock writes, cost-preserving --judge-only behaviour, branch-specific BYOK accounting, Observatory-backed ceiling reporting and Rollout-6 quality canary are also more operationally complete. X has the clearer owner's-estate role table and strong requirement traceability, but its four thinker artefact kinds lack equally complete output and integration contracts, D18 unconditionally adds cost fields and could double-count when upstream cost is already included, and Q4-Q17 leave many implementation decisions marked pending.
risks: Y never explicitly requires the deployed routine role to be Fable on subscription and worker/main to be Opus 5.5 on subscription; Rollout step 4 merely says to write real ids. X states this owner-specific mapping correctly.

Y's subscription --from-file degraded path still permits non-API meanings, and its 2,000,000-byte input limit and 32,000-token default output limit are compromises not established by the order and can conflict with unstinted key thinking.

Y assumes usage.is_byok and restricts the release to OpenAI-compatible chat completions; neither is established by the brief, so the real Fable and OpenRouter fixtures must validate those assumptions.

Y's estate_usd=max(observatory_usd, local_month_usd) can understate current estate spend when Observatory lags, rather than reliably representing all projects' totalUsd. Its null-cost recovery is also internally inconsistent: appending a manual record does not remove the original row that spend.py check will continue to fail.
